newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan doctors temporarily suspend strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan doctors temporarily suspend strike.

text.p: Venezuelan public doctors voted on Thursday to temporarily suspend a 13-day strike and return to work at hospital emergency rooms nationwide for a week.
The vote, passed at a meeting in the early hours after more than seven hours of angry debate, followed a government threat to start dismissing the strikers.
The 25,000 public sector doctors want their monthly take-home pay, including bonuses, to be increased from an average $304 to $1,000. The government has offered a 25 percent wage increase.

Authorities said the strike led to at least 15 deaths as doctors left some emergency rooms and intensive care units unattended after the stoppage began on Dec. 27. The government said negotiations would not begin until work resumed at emergency services.
Officials hoped the vote would help solve one of the worst crises in Venezuela's bloated public sector since President Rafael Caldera took office three years ago.
